Farmer's Carry, Farmer Carry Loaded Hike and Plate Pinch Hold all require a sustained crush or pinch grip against an external pulling load, the named provoking mechanism alongside wrist extension. Deliberately not extended to loaded-carry as a whole (Yoke Walk, Sandbag Bear Hug Carry, overhead carries load the shoulders/back and torso, not a sustained hand grip against a pull) and deliberately not extended to hangboard hangs or dead hangs, which load the finger flexor/pulley system in a fixed crimp, a different named mechanism already covered by this app's finger-pulley and trigger-finger rules; sweeping those in for tennis elbow too would repeat the over-broad grip pattern already found and fixed this week. Sourced (loaded gripping mechanism), unreviewed. Hangs and pull-ups are left to the finger-injury rules: the lateral epicondyle is the extensor origin, and the drafter's anatomical objection to sweeping flexor-loaded hangs into it stands. Sourced (mechanism), unreviewed.

Extends the existing hand-on-ground, wrist-extended, weight-bearing contraindications (Push-Up Plyo, Handstand Wall Hold, Wall Walk) to the rest of that same position family: every Push-Up variant, Bear Crawl, Renegade Row, Trapeze Plank Hold and Handstand Push Up all load a fully extended wrist under bodyweight, the exact position StatPearls names. Front-rack/goblet/Zercher/thruster and heavy curls were checked and NOT included: the wrist there is stabilizing a bar resting on the shoulders or forearm rather than bearing weight through an extended wrist joint, and no fetched source named that position or named curls for wrist sprain specifically, so including them would be wider than what was actually read. A generic 'Front Plank'/'Plank'/'Reverse Plank'/'Side Plank' entry was also left out because the catalog does not say whether it is performed on hands (wrist extended) or forearms (wrist neutral). Sourced (weight-bearing wrist extension mechanism), unreviewed.

Extends the existing hand-on-ground, wrist-extended, weight-bearing contraindications (Push-Up Plyo, Handstand Wall Hold, Wall Walk) to the rest of that same position family: every Push-Up variant, Bear Crawl, Renegade Row, Trapeze Plank Hold and Handstand Push Up all load a fully extended wrist under bodyweight, the exact position StatPearls names. Front-rack/goblet/Zercher/thruster and heavy curls were checked and NOT included: the wrist there is stabilizing a bar resting on the shoulders or forearm rather than bearing weight through an extended wrist joint, and no fetched source named that position or named curls for wrist sprain specifically, so including them would be wider than what was actually read. A generic 'Front Plank'/'Plank'/'Reverse Plank'/'Side Plank' entry was also left out because the catalog does not say whether it is performed on hands (wrist extended) or forearms (wrist neutral). Sourced (weight-bearing wrist extension mechanism), unreviewed.

Reverse Wrist Curl (Forearm Extensors) trains the exact structure named in the mechanism, the wrist extensors/ECRB. StatPearls names "progressive eccentric strengthening of the common extensor tendon" as the physical therapy intervention for lateral epicondylitis. This exercise already carries a prehab row for tennis-elbow in the catalog; adding rehab_early because eccentric extensor loading is the standard active-symptom treatment, not only prevention. Source: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK431092/

Seated Palms Up Wrist Curl (Dumbbell) matches the InformedHealth.org eccentric protocol verbatim: seated, arm resting on the thigh, palm facing upward, lowering the weighted hand under control. This is the flexor-side analog of Reverse Wrist Curl and is a different exercise from the existing (and mechanistically mismatched) prehab row this injury already carries for exercise 17, which trains extensors, not the flexor-pronator origin golfer's elbow actually involves. Source: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK507006/

Deadlift, good-morning, and rack-pull variants are, by definition, loaded forward bending under a lifted load, the mechanism AAOS names as aggravating. A blanket hip-hinge pattern rule would also sweep in low-flexion, low-risk hinge work (hip thrust, glute bridge) the mechanism does not name, so name_regex targets the loaded-forward-bend lift family specifically instead of the hip-hinge pattern. Sourced (loaded forward-bend lifting mechanism), unreviewed. The AAOS sentence asks for slow, controlled bending and lifting rather than forbidding it; this rule stands on the curated tier, which already contraindicates the conventional and Romanian deadlift, block pull, Zercher good morning and back squat for this injury, so the remaining deadlift, good morning and rack pull variants follow the movement class a human established. Sourced (mechanism), unreviewed.
